brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut by benchmarking to a maker — they're a pure reseller carrying a margin we can avoid — and line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% reduction, targeting the maker's price — their full revenue (100.0%) comes from reselling, so their price includes a middleman margin we shouldn't pay.
priceAsk.target: The market asks ₹0.55–1.20/pc for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume — anchor to the lower end of that band and push them to match it or lose the volume.
priceAsk.basis: They manufacture nothing (0.0% manufactured, 100.0% traded) — every rupee we pay carries a reseller markup. The market verdict says 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so there's room to move down, especially if we commit volume or ease tolerances.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 Days After Receipt — don't extend payment to them, because they already stretch their own suppliers to 105d (vs. 57d peer median), so they have plenty of float.

brief.financialLeverage: They're fragile: a money-health score of 2/10, in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.58), and they keep only 2.8% profit on every ₹100 sold. But your ₹65.27 L spend is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue — a meaningful slice that gives you room to ask. They pay their own suppliers in 105d (vs. 57d for peers), so cash isn't as tight as the score suggests, but there's a pending legal case and near-zero manufacturing (100.0% traded). Push firmly on price — citing the reseller margin and the market band — but don't squeeze so hard you tip a wobbly supplier; instead, use the ask to qualify a robust second source and shift volume if they won't move.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's biggest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — makes pharma bottles, caps, preforms in-house; top second-source candidate to bypass the reseller margin.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — strong capability in pharma containers and closures; a robust alternate.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A maker lead from public research (confidence Medium, pan-India) — verify capability and get a maker's quote to anchor the price ask; not yet qualified or priced.

risks: They're in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.58) with a 2/10 money-health score and a pending legal case — supply continuity is at risk; don't concentrate all volume here.
Profit margin is only 2.8% — a steep price cut could push them into loss and threaten supply; balance the price ask with a credible threat to move volume, not a squeeze that breaks them.
They're a pure trader (100.0% traded, 0.0% manufactured) with no pricing power upstream — if you push too hard without a second source lined up, they may simply walk away or cut quality.
Your ₹65.27 L is 1.19% of their revenue — meaningful but not dominant; they have other customers, so the volume lever is real but not overwhelming.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're reviewing our rigid-packaging strategy and need to close the gap between reseller pricing and what a manufacturer would charge — let's talk about a 10–15% reduction to keep this volume with you.
